title: Offer Acceptance Friction Log and Priority Mitigation Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures observed points of friction that block or delay candidate offer acceptance, ranks them by business impact, and provides a prioritized mitigation checklist with concrete owner-level actions. Aim: reduce offer decline rate and time-to-accept by 30% for IC and leadership roles over the next quarter.

Audience:
People Ops recruiters, hiring managers, total rewards, hiring enablement partners, and recruitment operations.

How to use this doc:
- Log each candidate offer incident (see "Friction Log" table below) as soon as an offer outcome changes.
- Triage weekly in the Offers Review sync (People Ops + Hiring managers).
- Assign immediate mitigations (owner + ETA) for high-impact items.
- Track resolved vs recurring friction; escalate systemic issues to HR leadership.

High-level hypothesis and signals:
- Hypothesis: most declines and long delays are caused by (1) compensation misalignment expectations, (2) offer packaging/benefits ambiguity for cross-border hires, and (3) process lag where multiple internal approvals slow down candidate response windows.
- Signals to watch: declining acceptance rate within X days of verbal offer (metric: accepted/extended within 7 days), median time from verbal to written offer, declined reasons distribution.

Friction Log (fields to capture per incident):
- Candidate-name-id (UID): internal stub (not PII in shared doc)
- Role and band
- Hiring manager and recruiter
- Date verbal offer given
- Date written offer delivered
- Outcome: accepted | declined | counter-offer | stalled
- Time to response (days)
- Primary friction reason (pick one): comp | timeline | benefits | visa | counter-offer | counter-party communication | paperwork | other
- Short narrative (1–2 lines)
- Immediate mitigation assigned (owner + ETA)
- Follow-up: permanent change? (Y/N)

(Example row)
- UID: CAND-2025-0297 | SWE2 | HM: Marco S. | Recruiter: Aisha P. | Verbal: 2025-06-01 | Written: 2025-06-03 | Outcome: stalled | Time to response: 8 days | Reason: comp | Narrative: candidate asked for equity clarifications and sign-on that were not included in initial docs | Mitigation: SR engagement (Liang) to re-calc equity, send revised offer 2025-06-05 | Follow-up: template update proposed

Priority mitigation matrix (how we pick work to fix):
- Priority A (15%+ lift to acceptance or blocking pipeline): systemic comp mismatches, legal/visa delays for priority hires, contract negotiation handoffs that require EM/GC. Triage immediately; owner from compensation or legal.
- Priority B (5–15% lift): ambiguous benefits, inconsistent messaging from hiring manager, approvals that add >3 business days. Set 48–72 hour SLA for mitigation.
- Priority C (<5% lift): paperwork copy errors, cosmetic template issues, rare candidate preference quirks. Track and batch for weekly cleanup.

Quick mitigation playbook (actionable steps by friction type):
- Comp (expected vs offered):
  - Do not send offers until comp pre-brief is logged in the candidate packet (recruiter responsibility).
  - If candidate pushes back, escalate to comp-owner (Priya) within 24 hours with an impact note.
  - Use the rapid equity re-calculator (Confluence link in linked_artifacts) and supply 2 variant options rather than open negotiation.
- Timeline/approvals:
  - Implement 'expedite flag' for senior hires—reduced approval chain until written offer sent (temporary delegated authority).
  - Recruiter to ping approvers on Slack and copy hiring manager; create a JIRA approval ticket for auditable trail.
- Benefits/International hires:
  - Include short benefits summary PDF in first outreach for cross-border candidates.
  - For APAC/EU hires, include localized PTO and taxes FAQ snippet.
- Counter-offers:
  - Ask candidate for timeline of counter-offer; request 48–72 hour close window.
  - If candidate engages with counter-offer, recruiter to run a "stay vs join" script with HM and outline non-comp reasons to join.
- Communication handoffs:
  - Standardize recruiter -> hiring manager offer brief (3 bullets: comp, must-haves, red flags).
  - Draft and store 3 templated message threads (verbal, written, follow-up) in HR templates library.

Outreach and message templates (short):
- Verbal-offer script (recruiter): "We are excited to offer you the [role] at Redwood Inference. Base compensation will be [X], equity [Y], sign-on [Z], and benefits include [summary]. Expect the formal offer in your inbox within 48 hours. How does that sound?"
- Offer follow-up (48-hour reminder): "Quick note—wanted to surface any questions on the offer packet. We can set time with hiring manager or compensation lead if you'd like a deep-dive. Our offer expires on [date]."
- Counter-offer close (if candidate says they're considering another offer): "We understand the consideration. To help you decide, can you share the aspects you value most? We can see if there's room to address them quickly."

Owner matrix (who does what):
- Recruiter: populate friction log entry, manage candidate communications, and assign immediate mitigations.
- Hiring manager: provide one clear hiring rationale bullet and priority list (must-haves vs nice-to-haves).
- Comp/Rewards: owner for comp escalations, equity calc, sign-on authority.
- Legal/People Ops: visa and contract templates; approve expedite flags.

Metrics and reporting (weekly):
- Acceptance rate by role band (rolling 30 days).
- Median days from verbal->written and written->accept.
- Top 5 friction reasons (count and proportion).
- Number of 'expedite flags' used and success rate.

Process changes proposed (short list for immediate adoption):
1) Add a required "Comp pre-brief" checkbox in the ATS candidate packet. (Owner: Recruiting Ops, ETA 2 weeks)
2) Pilot delegated approval for up to L5 offers to reduce approval chain (Owner: HR leadership, ETA 4 weeks)
3) Create localized benefits 1-pagers for top recruiting regions (Owner: People Ops, ETA 3 weeks)
4) Weekly offers retro (15 minutes) to review all stalled offers (>5 days) and assign mitigations. (Owner: People Ops)

Open questions and risks (notes to self):
- How to surface equity valuation quickly for multi-country offers where equity vehicle differs? Confluence link + comp owner needed.
- Risk: overly aggressive expedite flags could increase compliance exposure. Add guardrail: automated audit snapshot when flagging.

Next steps before next sync:
- Populate the friction log for all offers in last 30 days (people-ops team).
- Marco and Priya to draft expedited approval template and delegate language.
- Liang to prototype localized benefits one-pager for UK and India hires.

Appendix: quick checklist for recruiter before sending written offer:
- Comp pre-brief completed in ATS (yes/no)
- Candidate timezone & local benefits noted (yes/no)
- Visa/relocation flagged (yes/no)
- Hiring manager confirmation (yes/no)
- Expected sign-by date in offer (48–72h)

Notes and provenance:
- This is a working document — capture incidents liberally.
- Drafted after a hire retro (2025-06-05) where three offers stalled on comp clarity and one senior hire lost due to multi-day approval lag.
- We will convert resolved, recurring items into permanent ATS templates and Confluence SOPs.

Slack threads / PR references to copy into Confluence when finalized:
- #people-ops-offers: thread 2025-06-05 "offer-stall-retro"
- PR for ATS checkbox: GitHub HR-ops:pr/23

End of doc.
